payload.headline: Apple climbs 1.43% to 354.07, still priced above every value estimate

summary.thesis: Apple is a strong business whose cash flow is growing fast, but the 354.07 price needs faster growth than Apple is showing, and analysts' forecasts are slipping.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: wait. The price sits just under resistance with little room to rise, and the macro read is negative.
summary.act_at: Long-term buying from 300.56; swing only on a close above 361.87

payload.happening: Apple closed at 354.07, up 1.43% on the day. That puts it at the top of its recent trading range, just under resistance at 359.79–361.87. The only Apple news is a reported Amazon discount of almost $50 on six months of Apple TV, which is minor. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-28.
payload.business: The core business numbers are strong. Sales over the last twelve months were 478.8B, up from 416.2B. Free cash flow, the cash left after running and investing in the business, rose to 136.1B from 98.8B. Operating margin, the share of sales kept as operating profit, rose to 33.01% from 31.97%. Two numbers point the other way. Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.72% from 16.6% two quarters ago. Inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%. Unsold products can lead to price cuts and lower margins, so margins are what is at risk. Demand is still growing and cash generation is not at risk. The new investigation risk in the annual report is a governance and sentiment issue, and it does not change the business today. The Apple TV discount and the TikTok outage do not change the business.

worth.text: At 354.07, Apple trades at 39.4 times trailing earnings and 33.4 times next year's expected earnings. It also trades at 10.7 times sales, against a peer median of 5.2. That is at the 98th percentile of Apple's own last five years. A discounted cash flow model (DCF) values a company from its future cash. Ours gives 143.11 in the bear case, 198.72 in the base case and 260.24 in the bull case. Apple's own price-to-sales history gives 222.1 to 300.56. The gap comes down to one input: how fast free cash flow grows at the start. To justify today's price, it would have to start growing at about 26.8% a year. Sales grew 15% last year and 7.7% a year over three years. At 20% starting growth the value is 273.18. At 30% it is 399.83. My fair-value range is 143.11 to 300.56.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow has to start growing at about 26.8% a year to support the price, well above the 15% sales growth of last year.

bull: Free cash flow rose to 136.1B from 98.8B a year earlier, so the cash engine is getting stronger.
Operating margin improved to 33.01% from 31.97% even as sales grew, so profitability is not eroding yet.
The share count fell 1.56% over the year, so each share owns a bit more of the company.
bear: Price-to-sales of 10.7 is against a peer median of 5.2 and at the 98th percentile of Apple's own five years, which leaves little room for a miss.
Analysts cut next-quarter EPS (earnings per share) 3.8% in 30 days, to 2.15 from 2.24.
Inventory is up 154% while sales are up 12%. If margin falls to 24%, the model value drops to 204.49.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above the whole value range of 143.11–300.56, so it is too high to buy.
The top of my range and of Apple's own price-to-sales history, close to the rising 200-day average of 303.55. Buying starts here.
The value if free cash flow starts growing at 20%, which is still faster than last year's 15% sales growth. Adding makes sense here.

longterm.why: The business is high quality, but the price needs growth Apple is not showing, and forecasts are falling. The rule verdict is 'Too expensive' and the committee call is Hold.

swing.why: The price sits at 354.07–356.15, just below resistance at 359.79–361.87. That is less room than one typical daily move (ATR, average true range) of 8.32, and the macro read is negative. Enter only on a close above 361.87, or on a pullback that holds support at 347.89–351.46.

decision.timing: Options price a 5.3% move by 2026-12-18 and a 10.4% move by 2027-02-19, a window that includes the 2027-01-28 report. There is no long-term buy above 300.56 before that report shows whether the inventory build hurt margins.

change_mind: A drop to 300.56, near the 200-day average of 303.55, would put the price inside the value range and turn wait into buy.
If the 2027-01-28 report shows operating margin above 33.01% and next-quarter EPS estimates go back above 2.24, the higher growth cases (273.18 at 20% starting growth) become more credible.
A close above 361.87 would break resistance and turn the swing call from wait to enter.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait on both horizons, because the close of 354.07 remains above the 300.56 top of the value range.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
